I spent the evening with my friend who had the heart attack. He needed bypass surgery and came home Wednesday. Even though he has some house staff, he booked me to spend the evening with him so he could have some fun.

I did really enjoy our previous date, what there was of it, that is. He was also pleased and sorry it ended the way it did. So last night we had dinner (the cook cooked and I served) and after I cleared the table, we sat and talked for a little while. He asked questions about me and I asked about things he needed be to doing to recover.

He was kind of depressed about his health situation so I kept a cheerful face and flirted as occasions arose. I didn't want to overplay it of get him worked up. Then I got him bundled into his coat and we took a walk around the garden for some exercise. It wasn't too bad out, but you can tell it's going to be getting colder real soon.

When we back came in I put on some music and fixed some tea to warm us up. We played a board game and talked some more. He's basically on his own once the cook leaves for the night and is beginning to find that very depressing in and of itself. His family live too far out to visit and spend time with him during the week.

We watched a couple episodes of I Love Lucy and then watched a Bowery Boys movie. I had a great time. It was better than a most of the dates I had before college (which is when I stopped personal dating) and once I started "dating" professionally. It was worlds better than the last couple of evenings I spent club-hopping strip clubs.

He asked if I'd be willing to come back several days next week to keep him company. I accepted, of course. I like this man and wish he was 50 years younger. I can't tell if I like him because he's old or because he's smart and mature. Whatever. We had a pleasant evening.

Around 10:30 I waited in his bedroom while he got cleaned up and ready for bed, all the while talking about life and things he's done and seen and answering more questions about me and my life (not much to tell, comparatively). He's been around and I could have listened to him all night.

So after he got into bed I reset his monitor equipment for the day, made sure he had a pitcher of cold water, and tucked him in for the night. We said goodbye, I gave him a daughterly kiss on the cheek and left for home.

It may just be me, but I think his mood was sooo much better. He was smiling more and even laughing at things.

I'm looking forward to seeing him again tonight. I have time to visit the salon this morning, so I'm going to have my hair done in a 50's style. Something with big curls on top and maybe some long waves. I've got a really nice light blue cashmere pullover and cardigan set (I love Lands End sweaters), my pearls, and a pair of wide-legged slacks I picked up at a vintage shop. I spent more to have them tailored than they cost me, but now they fit me oh, so well ;-) That ought to make give me a 50's pretty girl look.
